Plot a Pairwise Comparison Heatmap

pc.plot.heatmap.Rd

Creates a heatmap that visually represents pairwise comparison results between models or methods. Each cell in the heatmap corresponds to the comparison value between two methods, helping to identify relative performance patterns.

pc.plot.heatmap(comparison_df, title = NULL, desired_order = NULL)

Arguments

comparison_df

A square data frame or matrix containing numeric values. Both row names and column names must correspond to method or model names.

title

An optional string specifying the title of the heatmap. If `NULL` or empty, no title will be displayed.

desired_order

An optional character vector defining the desired order of methods on both axes. If `NULL`, the default row/column order is used.

Value

A ggplot object representing the heatmap visualization. The object can be directly displayed with `print()` or saved using `ggsave()`.

Details

**Requirements:** - The rows of the data frame must have names corresponding to the methods being compared. In other words, both row names and column names must represent the same set of methods. - The title is optional. If `NULL` or an empty string, the heatmap will be displayed without a title.

Examples

comparison_df <- data.frame(
  Model_1 = c(14, 7, 9, 8),
  Model_2 = c(9, 14, 12, 10),
  Model_3 = c(5, 2, 14, 5),
  Model_4 = c(6, 4, 9, 14),
  row.names = c("Model_1", "Model_2", "Model_3", "Model_4")
)
desired_order <- c("Model_1", "Model_2", "Model_3", "Model_4")
heatmap_plot <- pc.plot.heatmap(
  comparison_df = comparison_df,
  title = "Model Comparison Heatmap",
  desired_order = desired_order
)
#> Error in as.data.frame(comparison_df) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Method1") %>%     tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -Method1, names_to = "Method2",         values_to = "Count"): could not find function "%>%"
print(heatmap_plot)
#> Error: object 'heatmap_plot' not found
